messages:
anya: Quick async Q — PR #4523 changes /v1/generate response shape and request params. Summary: add `served_model_chain` (array) alongside existing `served_model` (string) and introduce a new request param `model_selector` (object) that can include `{ id, region_hint, tier_hint, pin }`. Is this safe for backward compatibility and what rollout do we want? ping @mike @sanjay @irene

mike: short answer: additive fields are non-breaking in principle, but we constantly have clients that do strict schema validation. Suggestion: gate the new response shape behind a feature-flag header `X-Redwood-Resp-V=2` for canary first, and keep `served_model` until we deprecate. Also bump minor in SDKs and add a runtime warning header when v1 clients hit the v2 path.

sanjay: nit on request side: do we accept both legacy `model_hint` (string) and new `model_selector` (object)? I'd prefer: if `model_selector` present -> use it; else map legacy `model_hint` to `{ id: model_hint }`. That keeps server logic simple and backward compatible.

irene: fallback precedence question — current runtime effectively does: explicit pin > model id > model_hint > tier/region hints. With `model_selector` containing both `region_hint` and `tier_hint` we should be explicit. I propose precedence: `pin:true` > `id` > `region_hint` > `tier_hint` > default routing. That keeps region affinity higher than cost-tier. Thoughts?

mike: agree on precedence. Also request that `served_model_chain` reflect the exact routing attempts in order so it can be used to debug fallbacks, e.g. ["gpt-4-x","gpt-4-x-quant","gpt-3.5-econ"]. Make sure chain entries include variant IDs (quantized / fallback).

anya: here's a small sample response we plan to emit (when client opts in):
```json
{
  "id": "resp_123",
  "text": "...",
  "served_model": "gpt-4-x",
  "served_model_chain": ["gpt-4-x", "gpt-4-x-quant"]
}
```
This keeps `served_model` for existing clients and adds `served_model_chain` for observability.

irene: telemetry + warnings — rather than a custom header, can we include a `warnings` array in the JSON body for now? e.g. \"warnings\":[\"served_model will be deprecated in 30d\"]`. Less likely to be dropped by proxies and easier for SDKs to surface.

sanjay: rollout plan idea: 1) opt-in flag to 5% for 48h (collect parser/SDK errors), 2) if <0.1% client errors and no regression, 7d ramp to 50%, 3) final default after 30d with deprecation notices. I'll draft the canary config and add metrics to track `sdk_parse_error_count` and `served_model_chain_seen`.

mike: small API naming request in the PR comments: `pin` as a bare boolean is ambiguous. I suggested `prefer_pin` or `pin_preference` to make intent clear. Also please add unit tests that demonstrate legacy `model_hint` -> selector mapping. PR #4523 comments left.

anya: thanks — I'll update PR per comments (rename `pin`, add mapping test, embed example). Will add docs + changelog entry. Can we get devex to add SDK lint warnings for consumers parsing the whole response strictly? @devex-bot

deploy-bot: canary: PR #4523 deployed to 5% with tag `resp-v2-canary` at 2023-06-15T09:12:00Z (auto). Rolling window: 48h.

mike: code-review ping: if anyone on eng-platform is free can you take a quick pass on the updated tests and the `served_model_chain` serializer? small perf question on serializing chain for streaming responses.

anya: tagging this thread open — will update when PR changes landed. thanks all.
